title: Auxiliary variable valuation as an all-false prefix
statement: Fix an assignment $\alpha$ and a list of literals $\mathit{lits}$, and let $j$ be an index with $j + 2 \le |\mathit{lits}|$. Then the auxiliary variable valuation associated with $\alpha$, $\mathit{lits}$, and $j$ holds if and only if every one of the first $j + 2$ literals of $\mathit{lits}$ evaluates to false under $\alpha$.
replaced:
Provided $j + 2 \le |\mathit{lits}|$, \texttt{SATTo3SAT.extraVal} $\alpha$ $\mathit{lits}$ $j$
is logically equivalent to the condition that every element of $\mathit{lits}.\mathtt{take}(j+2)$
is false under $\alpha$.
